text:
Braeden Bowman went undrafted and earned his way to an NHL job, and in his second season he is still holding one: 25 games, 5 goals, 9 points. The minutes have slipped, though. He averages 12.65 a night for the season but 11.1 over the last ten games, with three nights under ten minutes.

Our numbers say he has deserved more points. Vegas has scored 6.4 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, and his own goals (5 on 5.3 expected) are right where they should be. At 5v5 the Golden Knights are close to even with him out there: 49.7% of the attempts, 51.6% of the expected goals.

His game is getting to the right spots. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him taking 1.4 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net last season, the kind that go in 25% of the time. He rarely carries the puck in (30% of his entries), so his line leans on dump-ins and the forecheck.

What to watch is the ice time, which has been falling while the bounces go against him.
